title: useRef initializers (Annotation.define / new Compartment) re-evaluated on every render
description: `useRef(Annotation.define<boolean>())` (251), `useRef(new Compartment())` (259) and `useRef(new Compartment())` (260) evaluate their argument on every render even though React keeps only the first result. Each render therefore allocates a throwaway Annotation type and two throwaway Compartment objects that are immediately discarded. The allocations are cheap so the runtime cost is negligible, but it is the well-known `useRef(eagerInit())` anti-pattern; the idiomatic lazy form is `useRef<T>()` populated on first use, or `useState(() => ...)[0]` / a `useMemo` with a stable init so the constructor runs once.
evidence: Line 251 `const externalSyncAnnotation = useRef(Annotation.define<boolean>())`; lines 259-260 `useRef(new Compartment())`. The expression inside useRef(...) is a function-call argument, so JS evaluates it on each render before useRef ignores it past the first.
est_reduction: 3 discarded allocations per render eliminated (no LOC change required if switched to a lazy-init helper)
behavior_preservation: Behavior-preserving: the retained ref values are identical; only the per-render throwaway allocations are removed.
